note: Layout Builder Browser replaces core's layout_builder.choose_block controller (via a RouteSubscriber at RoutingEvents::ALTER priority -110) with BrowserController::browse, which builds a curated block chooser out of two config entity types: layout_builder_browser_blockcat (categories: label, status, weight, opened, image_path, image_alt) and layout_builder_browser_block (block_id -> a block plugin id, category, label, status, weight, image_path, image_alt). Whether the takeover happens at all is decided by layout_builder_browser.settings:enabled_section_storages (ships as ['overrides']); the other two settings keys are use_modal and auto_added_reusable_block_content_bundles. The module defines NO permissions file (everything uses core's 'administer site configuration'), no plugin types, no Drush commands, and its only hook is hook_layout_builder_browser_alter(). Every medium/hard case is grounded in that real config: introspection reads back the live catalog entities and the live settings object; execution builds a real category + browser block and flips the real settings keys, verified against live config.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site the layout_builder_browser module is enabled but Layout Builder's 'Choose a block' screen still shows the normal core list when I edit the default layout of a content type. Which configuration object and key decides whether the custom browser is used, and what value does the module ship with?
evals.expected_output: layout_builder_browser.settings:enabled_section_storages lists the section storage plugin ids the browser takes over. It ships as ['overrides'] only, so per-entity layout overrides use the curated browser while the default-layout screen falls back to core's ChooseBlockController. Add 'defaults' to the list (Settings tab at /admin/config/content/layout-builder-browser/settings) to cover both.

evals.prompt: I want to restrict which blocks editors can place in Layout Builder using the layout_builder_browser module, grouped into my own categories. Which config entity types does the module define for this, and which property on the block entity points at the actual block plugin?
evals.expected_output: Two config entity types: layout_builder_browser_blockcat (a category - id, label, status, weight, opened, image_path, image_alt) and layout_builder_browser_block (an allowed block - id, block_id, category, label, status, weight, image_path, image_alt). The block_id property holds the block plugin id (e.g. system_powered_by_block, inline_block:bp_simple, block_content:<uuid>). Config names are layout_builder_browser.layout_builder_browser_blockcat.<id> and layout_builder_browser.layout_builder_browser_block.<id>. Only entities with status TRUE are rendered, and a category with no visible blocks is dropped from the output.

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal contrib module layout_builder_browser, I want a custom module to change the block browser's search placeholder text and collapse some categories. Which hook does layout_builder_browser provide for that, and what arguments does it receive?
evals.expected_output: Implement hook_layout_builder_browser_alter(array &$build, array $context). $build is the browser render array ($build['filter'] is the search element, $build['block_categories'][<id>] are the details elements with 'links'); $context contains section_storage, delta and region. It is invoked at the end of BrowserController::browse(), so only when the curated browser actually built.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a Layout Builder Browser category configured whose machine name starts with lbb_eval. Inspect the live configuration and tell me: the category's human-readable label, and which of the browser blocks assigned to that category is currently DISABLED (give its machine name).
evals.expected_output: The category is lbb_eval_cat, labelled 'LBB Eval Promotions' (weight 7, opened false). It holds two layout_builder_browser_block entities: lbb_eval_powered (block_id system_powered_by_block, status true) and lbb_eval_help (block_id help_block, status FALSE) - so lbb_eval_help is the disabled one. Readable via `drush cget layout_builder_browser.layout_builder_browser_block.lbb_eval_help` or by loading the layout_builder_browser_block storage.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, for which Layout Builder section storage(s) is the Layout Builder Browser currently active, and is it configured to open in a modal? Inspect the running site's configuration rather than assuming the module defaults.
evals.expected_output: layout_builder_browser.settings currently has enabled_section_storages: ['defaults'] (NOT the shipped default of ['overrides']), use_modal: true, and auto_added_reusable_block_content_bundles: ['basic']. So the browser is active only on the default-layout screen and renders in a modal. Discoverable with `drush cget layout_builder_browser.settings`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the layout_builder_browser module to curate the Layout Builder block chooser: create an enabled block category with the machine name lbb_task_hero and the label 'LBB Task Hero', then register the core 'Powered by Drupal' block (block plugin id system_powered_by_block) as an enabled browser block inside that category. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a layout_builder_browser_blockcat config entity {id: lbb_task_hero, label: 'LBB Task Hero', status: TRUE} and a layout_builder_browser_block config entity with block_id: system_powered_by_block, category: lbb_task_hero, status: TRUE (via the entity storages, exported config, or the forms under /admin/config/content/layout-builder-browser).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the curated Layout Builder block picker only kicks in when someone customises the layout of one individual page - on the screen where we set up the standard layout for a content type we still get the plain, uncurated list. Make the curated picker apply on both of those screens, and make it open in a pop-up window in the middle of the screen instead of the narrow panel that slides in from the side. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set layout_builder_browser.settings:enabled_section_storages to contain both 'defaults' and 'overrides', and use_modal to TRUE (Settings tab at /admin/config/content/layout-builder-browser/settings, or the config factory).
